title: Work schedules two weeks in advance
action: Employers would post hourly shifts 14 days in advance and let workers swap shifts voluntarily.

title: Childcare fees based on family income
action: A state would fund licensed childcare places where families pay an income-based share and the state pays providers the balance of an agreed rate.

title: Duplexes and small apartments near jobs and transit
action: Cities would allow duplexes and small apartment buildings on suitable lots with existing services near jobs and transit, using a predictable approval process.

title: Paid sick time for hourly workers
action: An employer or state program would let hourly workers earn paid sick time for hours worked, including part-time hours.

title: Evening and Saturday primary care
action: Community clinics would test evening and Saturday appointments and give patients the visit price or sliding fee when they book.

title: Review of unpaid wage claims
action: State labor agencies would assign each wage claim to one person and speed up cases with documented underpayments, giving workers and employers a chance to respond.

title: Bus service for early and late shifts
action: A transit agency and major employers would test a bus route that runs in both directions at the start of early shifts and the end of late shifts.

title: Emergency rent payments before eviction
action: A county would make small emergency rent payments in time for eligible households to cover a shortfall before eviction.

title: Annual minimum wage adjustments for inflation
action: A state would publish and apply an annual inflation adjustment to its minimum wage.

title: Rent listings that include mandatory fees
action: Housing agencies and landlords would test listings that include all mandatory monthly fees in the rent shown and list required move-in charges separately.

title: Pay and credentials for apprentices
action: Employers and training providers would offer apprenticeships with pay from the first day, published pay steps and a recognized credential.

title: Pay during family or medical leave
action: A state insurance program would replace pay during qualifying illness, new parenthood or family caregiving, with a higher percentage of pay replaced for lower earners.

title: School breakfast and lunch for every student
action: A state and a school district would cover breakfast and lunch for every student, with no family application or charge at the register.

title: Hospital bill assistance before collections
action: Hospitals would help patients check whether they qualify for financial assistance and decide the application before sending a bill to collections.

title: Phone review of delayed unemployment claims
action: When a first unemployment payment is delayed, a state agency would flag the claim for a trained examiner who could resolve missing information by phone.

title: Childcare on nights and weekends
action: Counties and employers with shift workers would buy reserved places from licensed childcare providers on nights and weekends and pay for staffing those hours.

title: Base pay ranges in job listings
action: Before asking people to apply, employers would publish the range of base pay they expect to offer and list tips, bonuses or commissions separately.

title: Car repairs needed to get to work
action: When a car breakdown threatens someone’s job and transit is unavailable, a local workforce agency would pay for essential repairs up to a limit, based on an independent quote.

title: Reusable rental screening reports
action: Participating landlords would accept the same screening report for 30 days if the renter authorizes it and can correct errors.

title: Insulation and air sealing in homes
action: Utilities and local housing programs would pay to insulate eligible homes and seal air leaks, including in rentals where tenants pay the energy bills.

title: Later pickup for after-school care
action: School districts and local providers would extend affordable after-school care to cover the time it takes families to get back from work.

title: Cash and insurance prices for prescriptions
action: Before checkout, participating pharmacies would show patients both the cash price and their insurance copay for the same drug and quantity.

title: Temporary payments when a raise ends a benefit
action: A state would test a payment that decreases over time for people whose modest pay raise would otherwise end a qualifying subsidy all at once.

title: Legal representation after an eviction notice
action: Counties would fund legal representation for eligible tenants as soon as they receive an eviction notice.

title: Daily and monthly caps on transit fares
action: Transit agencies would cap trip-by-trip charges at the price of the corresponding daily or monthly pass, including for riders who add cash to a fare card.

title: Counseling appointments with sliding fees
action: County clinics would contract for counseling appointments that people could book directly at a sliding fee, with some appointments outside work hours.

title: Matching grocery benefits spent on produce
action: Local food programs and grocers would match eligible grocery-benefit spending on fruits and vegetables up to a posted limit.

title: Respite care for family caregivers
action: Counties would buy hours of respite care that people could book to take a break from caring for an older or disabled relative.

title: Degree requirements in public-sector hiring
action: Public employers would remove degree requirements where the job does not need one, assess applicants against published job skills and keep required licenses in place.

title: Pedestrian crossings on routes to work
action: Cities would choose a crossing with people who use it and test a change suited to the site, such as adjusting signal timing, changing lighting or adding a pedestrian island.

title: Utility shutoffs during extreme heat or cold
action: Utilities and regulators would set heat and cold thresholds for pausing shutoffs and offer a way to repay overdue bills after the extreme weather passes.

title: Short-term premium help after job coverage ends
action: States would test short-term help with premiums for eligible people who lose job-based health coverage and are moving to another plan.

title: Paid heat breaks for outdoor workers
action: Employers and public contractors would test paid rest breaks, drinking water and accessible shade for outdoor workers based on heat conditions at the worksite.

title: Exam fees and starter tools for trades
action: Workforce boards would pay eligible exam fees and starter-tool costs before a worker’s first paycheck, while keeping employers’ existing obligations in place.

title: Deadlines for urgent rental repairs
action: City inspectors would prioritize urgent problems such as lost heat or water, set a repair deadline and verify with tenants that the work was done.

title: Vanpools for rural shift workers
action: Regional employers and transit providers would test vanpools timed to rural work shifts on routes without practical bus service.

title: Payroll savings without a workplace retirement plan
action: States would offer workers without a workplace plan a portable, low-fee retirement savings option through payroll, with fees clearly shown and an easy way to opt out.

title: Hearings on retaliation claims over worker organizing
action: Federal lawmakers would fund faster independent hearings for workers who report retaliation for organizing, with time for employers to respond.

title: Reusing documents for benefit applications
action: Benefits agencies would let applicants choose to reuse verified documents across programs where permitted, with phone and paper alternatives available.

title: Basic home internet with equipment included
action: Local governments would negotiate a low-cost home internet plan with providers that includes equipment and states the ongoing monthly price.

title: Urgent dental appointments for uninsured adults
action: Counties would buy urgent appointments at community dental clinics for uninsured adults, with a published sliding fee.

title: Evening and weekend tax filing help
action: Libraries and qualified tax-help providers would offer free filing appointments on evenings and weekends for eligible households.

title: Resale prices for land-trust starter homes
action: Local land trusts would keep ownership of the land and sell homes under a resale price formula that buyers can review before purchase.

title: Monthly child tax credit payments
action: A state would test an optional monthly payment of a refundable child tax credit, with an easy way to update income and a hardship process for overpayments.

title: Employee profit sharing
action: Employers would test a published formula for sharing profits on top of agreed base wages, include hourly staff and explain any period without a payout.
